meta.label: Shoes
meta.attribution: Reviewed 2026-06; curated from public sustainability reports, labor certifications, transparency sources, repair/resale programs, and fast-fashion risk reporting - not audited data. The greenest shoe is often the one you repair, resole, or simply keep wearing. Suggest changes via Contribute.

products.name: Nisolo

environment.note: Eco-Stylist says Nisolo lost its former sustainability standing after foreclosure, ownership change and hidden sustainability pages.

labor.note: Eco-Stylist reports that the former factory closed after foreclosure and current labor commitments are hard to verify.

transparency.note: Eco-Stylist says Nisolo's once-prominent sustainability pages were hidden after the 2025 ownership change, weakening current transparency.

durability.note: Leather footwear can be long-lived and repairable, but current public sources emphasize labels more than quantified durability outcomes.

accessibility.note: Nisolo sells premium direct-to-consumer footwear rather than budget mass-market shoes.

products.description: A formerly high-scoring ethical leather-shoe brand now treated as a caution case after foreclosure, ownership change and weaker transparency.

products.name: Veja

environment.note: VEJA says it uses organic cotton, Amazonian rubber and recycled materials as core sneaker inputs.

labor.note: VEJA describes direct producer relationships and fair-trade practices that cut out intermediaries and pay producers upfront.

transparency.note: VEJA publishes a dedicated project site explaining materials, supply chains, production limits and tradeoffs.

durability.note: VEJA is a solid everyday sneaker, but not a resole-first footwear system like Birkenstock or outdoor boots.

accessibility.note: VEJA is globally distributed but generally priced as a premium sneaker rather than a budget basic.

products.description: A French sneaker brand known for publishing unusually detailed sourcing information about organic cotton, Amazon rubber, leather and factories.

products.name: Ethletic
products.description: A German vegan sneaker brand built around Fairtrade cotton and FSC-certified natural rubber.

environment.note: Ethletic says its sneakers use Fairtrade organic cotton and FSC-certified natural rubber.

labor.note: Ethletic centers Fairtrade cotton and a producer premium model as its main labor/economic signal.

transparency.note: The brand publishes material, Fairtrade and FSC sourcing details in its sustainability pages.

durability.note: Canvas vulcanized sneakers can last, but the model is less resoleable than repair-first sandals or boots.

accessibility.note: Ethletic sells ethical sneakers at mid-range European prices, with outlet pricing sometimes available.

products.name: Icebug
products.description: A Swedish outdoor-footwear brand with strong climate reporting, B Corp certification, and durability focus.

environment.note: Icebug's B Corp profile says the brand offers climate-footprint transparency and is committed to halving emissions by 2030.

labor.note: Icebug has been a Fair Wear Foundation member since 2021, using third-party workplace inspections and reporting.

transparency.note: Icebug publishes sustainability indicators and supply-chain information for footwear models.

durability.note: The product line is technical trail and winter footwear built for rugged outdoor use rather than disposable fashion cycles.

accessibility.note: Icebug is premium outdoor footwear with narrower global retail reach than mass-market sneakers.

products.name: Patagonia Footwear

environment.note: Patagonia reports broad footprint progress including PFAS phaseout and Fair Trade factory coverage across its line.

labor.note: Patagonia says it pays a premium for Fair Trade Certified styles and reports tens of thousands of workers supported.

transparency.note: Patagonia publishes environmental and social footprint pages, though its current footwear offering is narrow.

durability.note: Patagonia's wading boots are built by Danner, and the company says some footwear soles can usually be replaced by a Vibram cobbler.

accessibility.note: Patagonia footwear is specialized, premium outdoor gear rather than everyday accessible footwear.

products.description: A narrow footwear case now centered on Patagonia wading boots and repair-backed outdoor gear, not everyday sneakers.

products.name: Vivobarefoot

environment.note: Vivobarefoot reports circularity work through ReVivo repair and refurbishment growth.

labor.note: Vivobarefoot says it is upgrading transparency and compliance among partners and suppliers, but wage disclosure is not leader-level.

transparency.note: Vivobarefoot's 2024/2025 integrated report publishes value-chain transparency and product-impact metrics, including its VMatrix scoring.

durability.note: ReVivo repairs, refurbishes and resells Vivobarefoot shoes, giving worn pairs a second-life route.

accessibility.note: Vivobarefoot shoes are premium-priced minimalist footwear with online/global availability.

products.description: A minimalist-footwear brand with a circularity push through ReVivo repair, resale and refurbishment.

products.name: Cariuma

environment.note: Commons rates Cariuma well for sustainable fibers, plastic-free packaging and some renewable-energy use, while still flagging missing emissions targets.

labor.note: Commons reports a supplier code of conduct, WRAP-certified production partners and traceability by tier, but not public supplier names.

transparency.note: Cariuma's public sustainability claims cover materials and reforestation, but supply-chain wage detail is thinner than transparency leaders.

durability.note: Cariuma sells everyday vulcanized sneakers; durability is decent, but the model is not built around resoling.

accessibility.note: Cariuma is mid-premium, mostly direct-to-consumer sneaker pricing.

products.description: A mid-priced sneaker brand using natural/recycled materials, B Corp certification and tree-planting as its main signals.

products.name: Allbirds

environment.note: Allbirds reports product carbon-footprint labeling and lower-impact material work across its sustainability program.

labor.note: Allbirds describes a global supplier network and partner responsibilities, but public wage disclosure is less detailed than labor-first brands.

transparency.note: Allbirds has labeled products with carbon footprints since 2020, using product-level climate disclosure as a consumer signal.

durability.note: Allbirds ReRun extends life through resale, but most styles are everyday sneakers rather than repairable/resoleable footwear.

accessibility.note: Allbirds is widely sold online and in stores at mid-market to premium prices.

products.description: A mainstream sustainable-sneaker brand that labels product carbon footprints and operates a resale channel.

products.name: Oboz
products.description: A hiking-footwear brand using B Corp governance, tree planting, and durability as its main values signals.

environment.note: Oboz says it has planted more than 7 million trees through its One More Tree program.

labor.note: Oboz uses B Corp standards as a governance/social-impact signal, but publishes less wage detail than Fairtrade or living-wage leaders.

transparency.note: Oboz publishes commitments around communities, climate, circularity and B Corp certification.

durability.note: Oboz designs technical hiking shoes and boots for trail durability rather than fashion turnover.

accessibility.note: Oboz is mid-premium outdoor footwear with broad US retail but less global reach than Nike or Adidas.

products.name: Thousand Fell
products.description: A sneaker brand designed around take-back recycling and bio-based/recycled materials.

environment.note: Thousand Fell's FAQ says each pair is backed by a no-landfill take-back program that breaks returns into reusable or downcycled materials.

labor.note: Public circularity claims are stronger than public labor disclosure; third-party summaries flag limited supply-chain information.

transparency.note: Materials and take-back are visible, but supplier/labor transparency is thinner than the best-scoring footwear brands.

durability.note: The model is designed for repeated everyday wear and end-of-life return, not traditional resoling.

accessibility.note: Thousand Fell is an online-first premium sneaker rather than a widely stocked budget option.

products.name: Birkenstock

environment.note: Birkenstock's value signal is long-lived cork/leather construction, but the brand is less impact-report-forward than sustainability leaders.

labor.note: Birkenstock highlights European/German production heritage, but public wage and supplier disclosure are limited.

transparency.note: Public product and care information is available, while social/environmental reporting is moderate compared with transparency leaders.

durability.note: Birkenstock says many sandals can be repaired through its repair service depending on article, size, material and damage.

accessibility.note: Birkenstocks are widely available at mid prices and can repay over time if repaired rather than replaced.

products.description: A durable cork-footbed sandal/footwear classic where repairability is the real sustainability signal.

products.name: Dr. Martens

environment.note: Dr. Martens says most outsoles use durable PVC and discusses product sustainability, but leather/PVC impacts remain meaningful.

labor.note: The company publishes modern slavery and sustainability reporting, but this is a mainstream supply-chain model rather than fair-labor leadership.

transparency.note: Dr. Martens publishes plc sustainability pages, but disclosure is moderate versus top transparency brands.

durability.note: ReWair restores and repairs pre-owned Dr. Martens footwear and bags for resale.

accessibility.note: Dr. Martens is globally recognizable and mid-premium priced, with both new and restored pairs available.

products.description: A durable boot brand with resale and repair efforts, but still leather/PVC-heavy and less transparent than leaders.

products.name: Danner
products.description: A premium boot brand whose strongest values signal is repair and recrafting rather than broad sustainability disclosure.

environment.note: Commons rates Danner insufficient for overall sustainability disclosure, so its strongest environmental signal remains repair/recrafting rather than broad impact reporting.

labor.note: Danner's California Transparency statement describes supplier audits, a code of conduct and follow-up inspections, but not living-wage leadership.

transparency.note: Commons rates Danner insufficient and says it could not find a dedicated sustainability page or annual report for a brand of this size.

durability.note: Danner offers rebuild and resole services that replace soles, recondition leather, repair stitching and hardware, and refresh laces/insoles.

accessibility.note: Danner is widely sold online and through outdoor/workwear channels, but premium boot pricing keeps access below mass-market sneakers.

products.name: KEEN

environment.note: KEEN says it removed PFAS from its shoes and sources leather from Leather Working Group-certified suppliers.

labor.note: The LWG tannery work includes environmental and social audits, but KEEN publishes less wage-level detail than labor-first footwear brands.

transparency.note: KEEN publicly explains its materials and Detox the Planet choices, though supply-chain wage disclosure is still moderate.

durability.note: KEEN's core outdoor footwear is designed for trail/work durability rather than fast-fashion turnover.

accessibility.note: KEEN is widely sold in outdoor retail and online at mid-to-premium prices.

products.description: A rugged outdoor-footwear brand with strong PFAS and leather-tannery work, but less public wage disclosure than labor leaders.

products.name: Timberland

environment.note: Timberland reports recycled, renewable and regenerative material work, including Earthkeepers materials, but remains a leather-heavy mainstream brand.

labor.note: Parent-company reporting provides supply-chain programs, but Timberland is not a labor-transparency leader at product level.

transparency.note: Timberland publishes responsibility and material information, though supplier/wage disclosure is less detailed than top ethical footwear brands.

durability.note: Timberland's classic boot value is longevity and repair-minded use rather than rapid sneaker replacement.

accessibility.note: Timberland is broadly available globally, including outlet and resale channels, at mid-to-premium prices.

products.description: A widely available boot brand with improving material work and real durability, but conventional scale and leather impacts.

products.name: Brooks Running

environment.note: Brooks' sustainable-consumption page tracks 2024 raw materials and sets goals for recycled/bio-based inputs, waste reduction and circular product.

labor.note: Fair Labor Association lists Brooks as building a responsible sourcing program around human rights and safe working conditions.

transparency.note: Brooks publishes a transparency hub and corporate responsibility reporting for materials, climate and sourcing progress.

durability.note: Running shoes are performance products with limited repairability; durability depends on mileage and model rather than resoling.

accessibility.note: Brooks is widely available through running stores and online, with premium but common pricing for technical running shoes.

products.description: A serious running-shoe brand with unusually visible climate/transparency work, but limited repairability by category.

products.name: Rothy's

environment.note: Rothy's says its knit-to-shape method creates less than 1% upper-material waste and uses recycled materials.

labor.note: Rothy's sustainability story is stronger on materials and factory waste than on public wage or third-party labor certification.

transparency.note: The brand publishes material/factory claims, but supply-chain labor transparency remains thinner than the leaders.

durability.note: Rothy's emphasizes washable shoes and durability testing, but products are not repair/resole systems.

accessibility.note: Rothy's is direct/retail premium footwear, more accessible than niche ethical brands but not budget.

products.description: A recycled-knit shoe brand with low-waste manufacturing and washable designs, but thinner public labor evidence.

products.name: Will's Vegan Store

environment.note: Will's Vegan Store says all products are vegan and its operations, including delivery and returns, are certified carbon neutral.

labor.note: The brand says its fashion collections are made in Italy and Portugal under European Union employment, discrimination, and health and safety law.

transparency.note: The public ethics page gives useful material and manufacturing claims, but less third-party labor detail than the strongest footwear leaders.

durability.note: Good On You notes long-lasting products, but the footwear is not a repair or resole system.

accessibility.note: Will's is a specialist vegan brand with online global reach but mid-to-premium pricing versus mass footwear.

products.description: A specialist vegan footwear option with carbon-neutral operations and EU manufacturing claims, though still less independently detailed on labor than top transparency leaders.

products.name: Etiko sneakers

environment.note: Etiko identifies certified organic cotton in its footwear and clothing and uses Fairtrade and GOTS/organic certification signals.

labor.note: Etiko markets its sneakers as Fairtrade-certified, including Fairtrade conditions for workers on certified sneaker lines.

transparency.note: The certification page gives unusually specific certification claims for cotton, Fairtrade, and organic inputs.

durability.note: Canvas sneaker construction is simple and repair-light; Etiko scores higher for ethics than for long-life repairability.

accessibility.note: Etiko is a smaller Australia-based ethical brand with online availability and moderate sneaker pricing, not mass-market distribution.

products.description: A strong ethical-sneaker niche: Fairtrade, vegan, organic-cotton focused, and better for labor-certification shoppers than for repair-first shoppers.

products.name: Wildling Shoes

environment.note: Wildling is a certified B Corp and frames minimal shoes around lowering impact across the value chain.

labor.note: B Corp certification covers company-wide social and governance standards, giving stronger labor accountability than an unaudited self-claim.

transparency.note: Wildling's B Corp profile and certification page provide third-party accountability signals for the whole organization.

durability.note: Minimal shoe construction can reduce material use and support everyday wear, but the products are not designed as conventional resoleable footwear.

accessibility.note: Wildling is a specialist minimalist brand with online reach and premium niche pricing rather than broad store availability.

products.description: A B Corp minimalist-shoe option for shoppers who want natural movement and lower-material footwear, with niche pricing and fit preferences.

products.name: Baabuk

environment.note: Baabuk is a certified B Corp making wool footwear, with an emphasis on natural materials and responsible production.

labor.note: B Corp certification gives company-wide social accountability; Baabuk also describes production in Nepal and Portugal.

transparency.note: Baabuk publicly explains its B Corp status and recertification path, a clearer accountability signal than a generic sustainability page.

durability.note: Wool slippers and sneakers are positioned for comfort and repeat use, but the brand is not primarily a repair/resole platform.

accessibility.note: Baabuk is a small specialist wool-footwear brand with premium pricing and narrower distribution than mainstream shoe brands.

products.description: A B Corp wool-footwear option, useful when shoppers want natural materials and comfort over vegan materials or low prices.

products.name: Hylo Athletics

environment.note: Hylo reports an 8.63 kg CO2e footprint for its IMPACT shoe, about 40% lower than industry average, and uses bio-based components.

labor.note: Hylo says it conducts regular supply-chain audits using independent third-party partners and SAC/Higg tools.

transparency.note: Hylo publishes B Corp status, a B Corp score, product carbon footprint, and audit-tool references for a flagship running shoe.

durability.note: Hylo says IMPACT is engineered to match or exceed traditional running-shoe durability, though running shoes remain mileage-limited products.

accessibility.note: Hylo is a premium performance-running brand sold online and through specialty channels, not a budget or mass-retail option.

products.description: A B Corp performance-running option with unusually specific product carbon and supply-chain audit claims, balanced by premium pricing and running-shoe replacement cycles.

products.name: Nothing New

environment.note: Nothing New says its sneakers use post-consumer recycled materials, including recycled plastic uppers, laces, labels, and liners.

labor.note: Commons credits recycled upper materials but flags limited production and labor reporting, so the labor score stays cautious.

transparency.note: The brand publishes material statistics, but Commons notes gaps in broader production reporting and improvement plans.

durability.note: Low-top recycled sneakers can be everyday shoes, but this is not a repair/resole system and durability evidence is limited.

accessibility.note: Nothing New is easier to buy and less expensive than many niche ethical shoes, while still above low-cost mass footwear.

products.description: A recognizable recycled-sneaker option with clear material claims, but much thinner labor and production transparency than the category leaders.

products.name: Native Shoes

environment.note: Native Shoes emphasizes animal-free footwear and the Remix Project for donating or grinding worn shoes into community materials.

labor.note: Native publishes lighter-footprint and recycling claims, but public labor and wage evidence is limited compared with certified leaders.

transparency.note: The brand explains its animal-free positioning and Remix program, while supplier-level transparency remains limited.

durability.note: Lightweight molded shoes can be practical for casual use, and Remix gives an end-of-life path, but they are not repairable footwear.

accessibility.note: Native is a more mainstream, family-friendly casual shoe brand with relatively accessible pricing and online retail availability.

products.description: A mainstream animal-free casual-shoe brand with a recycling story, useful for accessibility and end-of-life options but weak on labor disclosure.

products.name: Vessi

environment.note: Vessi says its shoes are PFAS-free and vegan, but independent brand-rating coverage flags limited sustainability reporting for its size.

labor.note: Vessi says its factories respect workers, but offers little public supplier, wage, or audit detail compared with certified leaders.

transparency.note: Commons rates Vessi low on accountability because it has not published the level of production information expected for a brand of its size.

durability.note: Waterproof knit shoes can serve a practical wet-weather niche, but the product is not repairable or resoleable.

accessibility.note: Vessi is a recognizable direct-to-consumer waterproof shoe brand with frequent availability and pricing below many niche ethical brands.

products.description: A highly searchable waterproof vegan-knit option, included with a cautious score because its public labor and accountability evidence is thin.

products.name: TOMS

environment.note: TOMS publishes environmental-policy goals and reports progress annually through its impact report.

labor.note: B Corp certification provides third-party social/environmental performance accountability, though not product-level living-wage proof.

transparency.note: TOMS says it publishes an annual Impact Report and uses B Corp standards for transparency and accountability.

durability.note: TOMS casual shoes are accessible everyday footwear but are not especially repairable or resole-centered.

accessibility.note: TOMS is broadly available through online and retail channels at mid-market prices.

products.description: A giving-focused B Corp shoe brand with impact reporting and broad access, but less durability than repairable footwear.

products.name: Crocs

environment.note: Crocs reports work toward bio-circular content in Classic Clogs, but the core material system remains foam/plastic-based.

labor.note: Crocs publishes corporate responsibility materials, but the brand is not a fair-labor or living-wage leader.

transparency.note: Crocs says its 2025 Comfort Report covers Inclusivity, Circularity, Climate and Community progress, alongside current bio-circular material targets.

durability.note: Classic clogs can be long-wearing and washable, but they are not repairable footwear.

accessibility.note: Crocs are widely available globally, often discounted, and very easy to find.

products.description: A very accessible, often durable clog route with improving material targets, but a foam/plastic footprint and weak repairability.

products.name: Skechers
products.description: A very accessible comfort-shoe giant with broad fit options and some packaging/material progress, but weak transparency and repair signals.

environment.note: Skechers reports some recycled-content styles and recyclable/FSC packaging, but its lower-impact Our Planet Matters line was only about 2.5% of 2024 production.

labor.note: Commons says Skechers shares limited supplier information and that its code of conduct does not ensure a living wage.

transparency.note: Shop Ethical reports Skechers scored 7/100 in the 2023 Fashion Transparency Index and 5/100 in Fashion Revolution's 2025 climate/energy disclosure benchmark.

durability.note: Skechers has many walking/work/comfort styles, but Commons reports no strategic program or service to keep products out of landfills.

accessibility.note: Skechers sells globally across women, men and kids, including wide/extra-wide, slip-in, walking, work and sale styles.

products.name: New Balance

environment.note: New Balance publishes 2030 targets for preferred midsole/outsole materials and science-based emissions cuts, with some 2025 goals still needing attention.

labor.note: New Balance publishes supply-chain social responsibility information and manages Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier lists.

transparency.note: New Balance reports supplier lists and impact reports, but disclosure remains partial relative to the highest-ranked transparency systems.

durability.note: New Balance makes durable athletic shoes and some US/UK-made lines, but most products are not resoleable or repair-system based.

accessibility.note: New Balance is widely distributed globally at mid to premium prices.

products.description: A mainstream athletic-footwear brand with public supplier reporting and some local-made lines, but conventional scale impacts.

products.name: Red Wing Shoes

environment.note: Red Wing says it has a climate roadmap for Scope 1, 2 and 3 reductions and reports energy, materials and leather-waste efforts.

labor.note: Red Wing says manufacturing facilities must pass social-compliance and code-of-conduct inspections before production and periodically afterward.

transparency.note: The company publishes impact and sustainability pages, but disclosure is less complete than brands with detailed annual footwear impact reports.

durability.note: Red Wing operates a repair shop and says many boots are repairable and some are resoleable, making longevity the main values signal.

accessibility.note: Red Wing is widely available through stores and work-boot channels, but pricing is premium compared with mass-market shoes.

products.description: A premium work-boot default whose best sustainability case is simple: buy once, maintain, resole, and keep wearing.

products.name: HOKA

environment.note: HOKA sets 2030 goals for less petrol-based plastic, lower footwear energy use and lower water use, though most running shoes remain synthetic performance products.

labor.note: HOKA states human-rights commitments aligned with ILO and UN frameworks, but does not provide living-wage proof at brand-leading depth.

transparency.note: Deckers publishes responsibility and Creating Change reporting for HOKA's parent company, giving more visibility than many mainstream shoe brands.

durability.note: HOKA shoes are performance running and walking products; durability is model- and mileage-dependent rather than repair/resole centered.

accessibility.note: HOKA is now widely sold through running stores, outdoor retailers and online channels, usually at premium running-shoe prices.

products.description: A highly accessible running and walking brand with useful impact goals, but conventional synthetic-shoe limits and little repairability.

products.name: On

environment.note: On's 2026-published 2025 impact update reports recycled/renewable midsole-material progress but also acknowledges absolute emissions pressure from growth.

labor.note: On's 2026 update says 80.9% of Tier 1 partners met its living-wage benchmark and that full Tier 1 coverage work was extended into 2026.

transparency.note: On publishes a transparency hub, supplier information and responsible-manufacturing policies covering traceability, standards and monitoring.

durability.note: On's 2026 update says it is moving from Cyclon into resale, donation and recycling while translating failure insights into circular design criteria.

accessibility.note: On is present in more than 80 countries, but prices sit in the premium running/lifestyle range.

products.description: A fast-growing premium running brand with strong transparency momentum and circularity pilots, balanced by growth and synthetic-material impacts.

products.name: Salomon

environment.note: Salomon's 2030 priorities include circular or eco-designed key products and a 30% absolute carbon-footprint reduction from a 2019 baseline.

labor.note: Salomon's June 2026 2025 impact report says 86% of Tier 1 suppliers achieved A or B ratings on its social-compliance standards.

transparency.note: Salomon publishes impact reports, supplier documents and certifications from its sustainability page.

durability.note: Salomon makes technical trail, hiking and winter footwear built for hard use, while most products remain replacement rather than repair systems.

accessibility.note: Salomon is globally distributed in outdoor and running channels, but prices are mostly premium compared with everyday shoe basics.

products.description: A technical mountain-sports brand with unusually visible circular-design and impact-reporting work for a mainstream outdoor shoe maker.

products.name: Merrell

environment.note: Merrell publishes recycled/organic/renewable material goals and examples, but independent ratings still flag incomplete brand-level reporting.

labor.note: Parent company Wolverine requires suppliers to follow its Production Code of Conduct, but Merrell has limited public wage and factory-level evidence.

transparency.note: Commons rates Merrell poorly on sustainability transparency because brand-level reporting is incomplete for a company of its size.

durability.note: Merrell is known for hiking and outdoor footwear and backs shoes with a one-year limited warranty, but it is not a resole-first system.

accessibility.note: Merrell is widely available through outdoor retailers and online, with many sale and mid-market hiking styles.

products.description: A practical mainstream hiking-shoe choice with broad access and useful durability, held back by weak brand-level transparency.

products.name: Repair or resole existing shoes
products.description: The highest-leverage shoe option when the pair you already own is repairable: soles, heels, straps, stitching and care can add years.

environment.note: Vibram's Repair If You Care campaign frames resoling and reuse as a way to reduce footwear waste and extend product life.

labor.note: Vibram's repair campaign routes resoling through certified cobblers, keeping repair labor in play while extending footwear life.

transparency.note: Repair is inspectable pair-by-pair: iFixit documents common shoe repairs, while cobblers quote visible work before replacement.

durability.note: iFixit notes many traditional dress shoes can be repaired by cobblers, especially heels and soles.

accessibility.note: Repair access depends on shoe construction and local cobbler availability; many cemented athletic shoes are less repairable.

products.name: Secondhand shoes
products.description: A lower-impact route when you can inspect condition, fit and remaining sole life, especially for durable leather, boots and lightly worn sneakers.

environment.note: ThredUp's 2026 resale report says secondhand represented roughly 10% of global apparel spend and is growing faster than retail.

labor.note: Buying used avoids triggering a new pair's manufacturing labor demand, though resale platform and logistics labor still matter.

transparency.note: Secondhand condition, wear and authenticity are seller-dependent, so transparency is only as good as photos, platform rules and inspection.

durability.note: Secondhand works best for high-quality shoes with repairable construction; worn foam sneakers can have little useful life left.

accessibility.note: Resale and thrift routes are widely available online and locally, often with lower prices than new shoes.

products.name: ReVivo by Vivobarefoot
products.description: Vivobarefoot's repair, resale and recycling route for buying refurbished barefoot shoes instead of automatically buying new.

environment.note: Vivobarefoot says ReVivo refurbishes returned Vivos and recycles pairs it cannot repair to at least Good condition.

labor.note: Refurbishment shifts some value toward repair work and away from new-pair manufacturing, but it does not fully audit original footwear labor.

transparency.note: ReVivo explains its role as a footwear repair service and refurbished footwear sales platform.

durability.note: Returned shoes are cleaned, repaired and graded before resale, with repair offered as a parallel route.

accessibility.note: ReVivo refurbished stock is priced below new Vivos, but availability depends on returned inventory and barefoot-shoe fit needs.

products.name: Dr. Martens ReWair
products.description: A Dr. Martens resale route for restored secondhand boots and shoes, useful when you want that style without buying a fully new pair.

environment.note: ReWair sells gently used and secondhand Dr. Martens at reduced prices instead of treating returned or worn pairs as waste.

labor.note: Refurbished resale can reduce demand for new production, while not verifying the original footwear supply-chain labor.

transparency.note: ReWair's FAQ explains that restored pairs receive a final quality check before resale.

durability.note: The program relies on Dr. Martens' durable boot construction and restoration, though pair condition still varies.

accessibility.note: Reduced prices improve access compared with new Dr. Martens, but inventory is US-limited and size/style availability varies.

products.name: REI Re/Supply footwear
products.description: A used-gear route for outdoor shoes and boots, strongest when it keeps functional footwear in use for hiking, camping and everyday outdoor needs.

environment.note: REI Re/Supply is built around shopping and trading in used gear, keeping functional outdoor goods in circulation.

labor.note: Used-gear resale can lower demand for new outdoor footwear production, though it does not verify original supply-chain labor.

transparency.note: REI explains the Re/Supply trade-in process and accepts gently used gear that is still functional.

durability.note: Used outdoor footwear is useful when the sole, upper and support still have real life left, but condition varies by item.

accessibility.note: REI members can shop used gear and trade in eligible items, but access depends on REI membership, stores and available inventory.

products.name: eBay pre-owned shoes
products.description: A broad secondhand route for shoes and sneakers, best when buyers check condition, fit, return terms and remaining sole life carefully.

environment.note: eBay enables pre-owned shoe resale, which can reduce new-pair demand when it replaces a new purchase.

labor.note: Buying used avoids commissioning a new pair but does not verify labor conditions behind the original footwear.

transparency.note: eBay's sneaker authenticity guarantee covers eligible new or pre-owned shoes above its threshold, but ordinary listings depend on seller detail.

durability.note: Condition varies widely, so buyers need photos, return terms and age checks, especially for foam sneakers and old adhesives.

accessibility.note: eBay's large marketplace and filters make pre-owned shoes easy to find across many price points.

products.name: Poshmark shoes
products.description: A mainstream app-based route for buying and selling secondhand shoes, with strong access but seller-dependent quality and transparency.

environment.note: Poshmark's marketplace includes new and secondhand shoes, so impact depends on choosing pre-owned items that replace new purchases.

labor.note: Resale can reduce new-production pressure, but it does not verify the original footwear labor conditions.

transparency.note: Listing quality, condition disclosure and seller behavior vary across a social marketplace.

durability.note: Durability depends on the original shoe, photos, seller condition notes and whether the pair has meaningful life left.

accessibility.note: Poshmark is a large app-based marketplace for buying and selling fashion, including shoes, across many price points.

products.name: GOAT used sneakers
products.description: A sneaker-resale route that supports used listings, useful for hard-to-find pairs but weaker when it fuels hype-driven collecting.

environment.note: GOAT allows selling new and used sneakers, apparel and accessories, but the environmental value depends on used purchases replacing new demand.

labor.note: Sneaker resale does not verify labor conditions behind the original shoes and can amplify demand for scarce new releases.

transparency.note: GOAT's selling terms describe item review, replica rejection and condition mismatches, giving more structure than informal resale.

durability.note: Used sneaker durability depends on age, materials, storage and sole condition, especially for older collectible pairs.

accessibility.note: GOAT gives access to hard-to-find sneakers, but prices, fees and collectible demand can make it less accessible than local secondhand.

products.name: StockX sneakers
products.description: A highly recognizable sneaker marketplace; useful to compare honestly because much of the model is still new/deadstock consumption rather than low-impact reuse.

environment.note: StockX's Verified Marketplace requires brand-new items, while newer Listings may include used items, so the route is not primarily a reuse option.

labor.note: A marketplace for new/deadstock sneakers does not improve original footwear labor conditions and can feed demand for new drops.

transparency.note: StockX explains its verification process and buyer promise, giving stronger transaction transparency than informal resale.

durability.note: StockX warns that sneakers five years or older may have structural weakness and reduced durability regardless of storage.

accessibility.note: StockX is easy to search and verify, but market pricing can be expensive for scarce or hype-driven shoes.

products.name: Vestiaire Collective shoes
products.description: A designer secondhand route for shoes, strongest when it replaces a new luxury or trend purchase rather than encouraging more collecting.

environment.note: Vestiaire sells pre-loved fashion, including shoes, and frames resale as part of circular fashion.

labor.note: Luxury resale can reduce new-production demand, but it does not verify labor conditions behind the original shoes.

transparency.note: Vestiaire advertises authentication and a large pre-loved marketplace, though item history still depends on seller and platform checks.

durability.note: Designer resale can favor repairable or longer-lived materials, but used shoe condition remains a practical risk.

accessibility.note: Vestiaire can lower luxury prices but remains less accessible than thrift, local resale or broad secondhand platforms.

products.name: Cobblers Direct
products.description: A US mail-in and drop-off repair route for shoes, boots, handbags and belts, useful when local cobbler access is weak.

environment.note: Cobblers Direct's model is explicitly shoe and boot repair rather than replacement.

labor.note: The service routes spending toward cobbler labor and repair skill instead of new footwear production.

transparency.note: Cobblers Direct explains its online process, repair consultation and mail-in/drop-off options.

durability.note: Repair work can replace soles, heels and damaged components, extending the life of pairs that still fit.

accessibility.note: Mail-in labels and DSW drop-off options make repair easier than finding an independent cobbler, though price and turnaround still matter.

products.name: NuShoe repair
products.description: A long-running US mail-in shoe repair and renewal service, useful for boots, sandals and shoes with enough structure to justify repair.

environment.note: NuShoe says it has restored more than 5 million pairs of boots, shoes and sandals since 1994.

labor.note: Shoe renewal channels spend to repair craftsmanship rather than only new footwear production.

transparency.note: NuShoe publicly describes its mail-in repair and restoration services, though quotes and suitability are pair-specific.

durability.note: Its renewal work is designed to preserve favorite footwear with repair and original manufacturer materials where possible.

accessibility.note: Mail-in repair improves access beyond local cobblers, but repair value depends on shoe construction, price and turnaround.

products.name: Vibram Sole Factor
products.description: A resoling and customization route centered on Vibram soles, useful when the upper still works but the outsole is worn or unsuitable.

environment.note: Vibram's Repair If You Care campaign promotes resoling and repair through selected cobblers to extend footwear life.

labor.note: Authorized cobbler work supports repair skill and local service labor instead of replacing the whole pair.

transparency.note: Vibram describes Sole Factor customization and repair services through its academy and partner stores.

durability.note: Resolings can add durable outsoles to boots, outdoor shoes and some sneakers when the upper is still usable.

accessibility.note: Access depends on compatible shoe construction and authorized repair availability, so it is less universal than broad resale.

products.name: Timpson shoe repairs
products.description: A UK high-street shoe-repair route with unusually broad access and a notable employment model for people facing barriers to work.

environment.note: Timpson offers in-store and warehouse shoe repairs across the UK, extending usable footwear life.

labor.note: The Timpson Foundation says Timpson is one of the UK's largest employers of ex-offenders and supports care leavers and other marginalized groups.

transparency.note: Timpson publishes repair-service details and foundation information, giving clearer social-purpose evidence than most repair chains.

durability.note: The shoe-repair service covers simple in-store work and more complex repairs sent to a central warehouse.

accessibility.note: Timpson advertises nationwide UK coverage through high-street shops, supermarket concessions and car-park pods.

products.name: Chaco
products.description: A repairable sandal route with a real resole/restrap program, strongest when you actually use ReChaco instead of replacing pairs.

environment.note: Chaco says its webbings use recycled plastic and highlights recycled-bottle REPREVE fiber in many products.

labor.note: Parent company Wolverine publishes general responsible-sourcing commitments, but Chaco-specific living-wage evidence is limited.

transparency.note: Commons rates Chacos poorly on accountability because it has not published the production and sustainability information expected for its size.

durability.note: ReChaco repairs sandals with resoling, restrapping and new webbings through an official repair center.

accessibility.note: Chaco sandals are widely sold in outdoor retail, but prices are mid to premium and repair shipping adds friction.

products.name: Xero Shoes
products.description: A minimalist/barefoot shoe route with strong low-material logic and warranty signals, but still meaningful synthetic-material tradeoffs.

environment.note: Commons rates Xero Shoes Fair, noting verified emissions measurement and waste-reduction steps but continued reliance on higher-emissions materials.

labor.note: Commons does not identify Xero as a labor leader; public supply-chain wage evidence remains limited.

transparency.note: Commons says Xero measures emissions impact and has third-party verification, but material plans and supply-chain detail remain incomplete.

durability.note: Commons notes Xero helps keep products out of landfill by offering a warranty, supporting a moderate durability score.

accessibility.note: Xero sells minimalist shoes across North America, Europe, Asia and Australia, with prices below many premium ethical brands.

products.name: Puma
products.description: A mainstream athletic-shoe brand with stronger reporting than many peers, still limited by global scale and conventional product churn.

environment.note: Commons rates Puma Good, citing active steps on products, operations and emissions plus thorough reporting.

labor.note: FLA's 2024 post-accreditation report says PUMA scored over 90% across six evaluated labor-program principles in its 2023-2024 review.

transparency.note: Puma publishes annual sustainability reporting and explains product, supplier and material initiatives through its sustainability hub.

durability.note: Puma helps address end-of-life through RE:FIBRE take-back, but most shoes are still conventional athletic products rather than repairable footwear.

accessibility.note: Puma is widely sold globally across discount, midrange and performance footwear channels.

products.name: ASICS
products.description: A mainstream running-shoe brand with notable climate and supplier-energy progress, but limited repairability and mixed independent ratings.

environment.note: ASICS reported a 43.1% reduction in direct-operations CO2 from 2015 and more than 50% recycled polyester material use in 2024.

labor.note: ASICS says it conducts due diligence and strictly prohibits human-rights and environmental violations across products and materials.

transparency.note: ASICS publishes sustainability reports and supply-chain reporting, including human-rights and transparency sections.

durability.note: ASICS performance footwear is model- and mileage-dependent; its NIMBUS MIRAI take-back shoe is notable but not yet the whole line.

accessibility.note: ASICS is widely sold through running, sporting-goods and online channels at mid to premium prices.

products.name: Saucony
products.description: A mainstream running brand with some recycled-material goals and durable performance models, but limited brand-specific labor and transparency evidence.

environment.note: Saucony says it aims for 90% of upper materials to be recycled, renewable or organic by 2025 and all preferred materials by 2030.

labor.note: Parent company Wolverine Worldwide publishes responsible-sourcing commitments, but public Saucony-specific living-wage evidence is limited.

transparency.note: Good On You rates Saucony Not Good Enough, citing gaps in public information across several impact areas.

durability.note: Saucony performance footwear can be durable for running use, but longevity is model- and mileage-dependent and not repair-system-led.

accessibility.note: Saucony is widely sold through running, sporting-goods and online channels at mid to premium prices.

products.name: Clarks
products.description: A widely available comfort and school-shoe default with some material initiatives and care guidance, but weak independent ratings and limited deep supply-chain disclosure.

environment.note: Clarks highlights recycled and lower-impact materials through its Every Move Matters program, including Origin 2.0 uppers made with 74% recycled content.

labor.note: Clarks' 2025 modern slavery statement says footwear came from 64 factories, about 40% direct-managed and 60% through agents, with audit and escalation processes.

transparency.note: The Commons gives Clarks a weak rating, reflecting limited public performance evidence despite some sustainability claims.

durability.note: Clarks emphasizes care and cleaning products to extend the life of existing shoes, though many models are not resole-centered.

accessibility.note: Clarks is broadly available in comfort, dress and school-shoe categories across stores and online channels.

products.name: Vans
products.description: A highly accessible skate and casual default with some parent-company reporting, but weak brand-specific disclosure and no strong repair model.

environment.note: Vans states a goal for its top four CO2-impact materials to be regenerative, responsibly sourced, renewable or recycled by 2030.

labor.note: Parent company VF publishes responsibility reporting and a factory list, but Vans-specific wage and remedy evidence remains limited.

transparency.note: The Commons rates Vans poorly, noting that brand-specific sustainability information is limited because reporting is mostly parent-company level.

durability.note: Vans' canvas-and-rubber skate styles are iconic everyday shoes, but most pairs are not designed around resoling or formal repair.

accessibility.note: Vans is globally distributed and commonly available through brand stores, mall retail, skate shops and online channels.

products.name: Converse
products.description: A globally accessible canvas-sneaker default with parent-company sustainability reporting, but limited brand-specific labor evidence and middling durability.

environment.note: The Commons rates Converse in the middle tier, citing some lower-impact material work alongside continued room for improvement.

labor.note: Converse benefits from Nike group supplier and sustainability reporting, but public Converse-specific living-wage evidence is limited.

transparency.note: Nike's reporting archive and manufacturing map disclose group-level sustainability and supply-chain information that covers Converse.

durability.note: Converse classics such as Chuck Taylor and Chuck 70 are long-running casual styles, but most are not built around formal repair or resoling.

accessibility.note: Converse is globally sold through its own channels and mainstream footwear retailers, with frequent entry-level and sale pricing.

products.name: Reebok
products.description: A widely available athletic and lifestyle brand that scores low because public sustainability, supplier and labor evidence is thin relative to its scale.

environment.note: The Commons rates Reebok poorly, citing limited public evidence on material impacts and broader environmental performance.

labor.note: Reebok posts a California Transparency in Supply Chains Act statement, but independent public evidence on wages, remediation and auditing is limited.

transparency.note: The Commons and other independent directories flag Reebok for weak public disclosure compared with better-reporting footwear peers.

durability.note: Reebok sells mainstream athletic and lifestyle shoes, but most models are not repair-centered and durability varies widely by use.

accessibility.note: Reebok remains broadly available online and through mainstream retail, often with discount pricing.

products.name: Under Armour
products.description: A mainstream performance-footwear option with more formal sustainability and FLA-linked labor infrastructure than some peers, but limited repairability.

environment.note: Under Armour publishes sustainability goals and impact reporting, but its performance-footwear footprint remains material- and volume-intensive.

labor.note: Under Armour is affiliated with the Fair Labor Association, which provides external oversight of code and supplier-labor systems.

transparency.note: Under Armour's current sustainability strategy page links impact reporting, a 2026 modern slavery statement, 2025 Tier 1 supplier disclosure and supplier-code materials.

durability.note: Under Armour footwear is designed for performance use, but durability varies by sport and model and the line is not repair-centered.

accessibility.note: Under Armour footwear is widely available through brand, sporting-goods and online retail channels at mainstream price points.

products.name: Adidas

environment.note: Adidas' 2026-published 2025 Annual Report combines financial and sustainability information, including an ESRS sustainability statement with limited assurance.

labor.note: Adidas is Fair Labor Association accredited and covers final-production suppliers under FLA oversight.

transparency.note: Adidas says it has disclosed global factory lists with supplier names and locations since 2007.

durability.note: Adidas footwear durability varies by model and is generally not repair/resole centered.

accessibility.note: Adidas shoes are available globally across discount, mid-market and premium tiers.

products.description: A global sportswear giant with better-than-average supplier transparency, still carrying mass-production impacts and labor-risk scrutiny.

products.name: Nike

environment.note: Nike publishes sustainability focus areas and FY24 sustainability data, but footwear scale makes absolute impact large.

labor.note: Nike publishes impact reporting and a manufacturing map, improving oversight, while its global supplier scale keeps labor scrutiny relevant.

transparency.note: Nike publishes supplier and sustainability data, but it is still a large conventional supply-chain brand rather than a transparency leader.

durability.note: Nike shoe durability varies by model and most pairs are not built around resoling or long repair loops.

accessibility.note: Nike is available globally across broad price tiers and resale/discount channels.

products.description: The global athletic-shoe default: huge access and published impact data, with scale, labor and material impacts that remain substantial.

products.name: Teva

environment.note: Teva says its straps use recycled polyester and reports large volumes of PET bottles and post-industrial fiber repurposed into products.

labor.note: Parent company Deckers publishes supplier policies and modern-slavery statements, but Teva is not a living-wage proof brand.

transparency.note: Deckers' policy hub publishes ethical supply-chain, environmental, animal-welfare and modern-slavery documents for the brand portfolio.

durability.note: Teva sandals are built for outdoor wear and the TevaForever program gives worn sandals an end-of-life route, but most models are not repair-centered.

accessibility.note: Teva is broadly available through outdoor, shoe and online retailers at mainstream sandal prices.

products.description: A mainstream outdoor-sandal choice with recycled-strap and take-back signals, though not a full repair-first footwear model.

products.name: OluKai

environment.note: OluKai says it selects durable materials and uses responsible leather and rubber choices in sandals, shoes and slippers.

labor.note: B Lab lists OluKai as a Certified B Corporation, giving it a stronger verified governance signal than ordinary sandal brands.

transparency.note: OluKai's B Corp profile and brand pages describe community giving and responsible-material claims, but product-level factory disclosure is limited.

durability.note: The brand emphasizes quality, comfort and durable materials, but it does not present the same repair infrastructure as Chaco or Bedrock.

accessibility.note: OluKai is widely sold in US outdoor and footwear retail, but at premium sandal and casual-shoe prices.

products.description: A premium sandal and casual-shoe brand with B Corp and give-back signals, best viewed as a values-improved mainstream choice rather than a repair leader.

products.name: Blundstone

environment.note: Blundstone's Every Step Better program sets quality, resource-use and footprint commitments, but Commons notes mixed materials and limited recent progress reporting.

labor.note: Blundstone says people making its product should be employed ethically and free from exploitation, but public evidence remains policy-led rather than worker-outcome proof.

transparency.note: Blundstone publishes commitments, values and partner expectations, while third-party ratings still flag limited detail on materials and recent performance.

durability.note: Blundstone designs around durability and comfort, but its own support page says many ranges are not made to facilitate resoling.

accessibility.note: The brand is widely available in the US, UK, EU and other markets as a mainstream premium Chelsea/work-boot option.

products.description: A durable everyday boot benchmark with strong real-world wear appeal, but weaker resoling and transparency than repair-first bootmakers.

products.name: ECCO

environment.note: ECCO reports waste recovery in shoe factories and tanneries and says it works on water recycling and carbon reduction.

labor.note: ECCO publishes responsibility policies and animal-welfare/leather sourcing detail, but public labor-outcome evidence is limited.

transparency.note: ECCO discloses ownership of four tanneries and says all are Leather Working Group Gold rated and audited bi-yearly.

durability.note: ECCO is known for comfort and leather craft, but most models are mainstream glued or molded footwear rather than easy-resole designs.

accessibility.note: ECCO footwear is globally distributed through brand stores, online retail and department-store channels.

products.description: A comfort-footwear mainstream option with unusually visible tannery ownership and LWG leather signals, but limited repairability.

products.name: NPS Solovair

environment.note: Solovair says all NPS factory footwear uses Goodyear welting so soles can be replaced when uppers are cared for, supporting long use.

labor.note: The official store says Solovair is made in Wollaston, Northamptonshire, with production techniques carried out in the NPS factory.

transparency.note: NPS publishes made-in-England, factory-tour, Goodyear-welting and repairs pages, giving more construction transparency than many boot brands.

durability.note: Solovair repair guidance says the footwear can be resoled if the upper and welt are in good condition, with replacement soles available.

accessibility.note: Solovair is sold online internationally, but price, sizing and repair logistics make it less accessible than mass-market boots.

products.description: A repairable, Goodyear-welted boot and shoe path for shoppers prioritizing long life over low upfront price.

products.name: Bedrock Sandals

environment.note: Bedrock's Re-Soul & Repair program replaces worn sole units and repairs straps, extending the life of sandals instead of replacing the full pair.

labor.note: Bedrock provides repair and warranty infrastructure, but public labor and supplier disclosure is thinner than certified labor leaders.

transparency.note: The repair pages clearly explain available repair/resole services, timing and customer process, giving unusually practical lifecycle transparency.

durability.note: Bedrock says its Re-Soul program launched in 2016 and can replace the full sole unit while keeping the worn-in straps.

accessibility.note: Bedrock is a smaller direct-to-consumer adventure-sandal brand, with higher prices and narrower fit needs than mainstream sandals.

products.description: A high-signal sandal option for people who want a warm-weather pair with an actual repair and resole pathway.

products.name: Thorogood

environment.note: Thorogood's strongest environmental signal is repair/restoration of leather work boots rather than low-impact materials.

labor.note: Thorogood's American Union series is explicitly union-made, but not every Thorogood model carries the same US/union-made signal.

transparency.note: Thorogood publishes union-made, repair/restoration, care and dealer information, though sustainability reporting is narrower than B Corp or audited leaders.

durability.note: Thorogood advises resoling or restoration to extend work-boot life and frames restoration as more cost-effective than replacement.

accessibility.note: Thorogood boots are available through workwear dealers and online retail, but at work-boot prices and with model-specific safety features.

products.description: A useful work-boot addition: not low-impact by material, but stronger on union-made options and repairable long-use construction.

products.name: Allen Edmonds

environment.note: Allen Edmonds frames its recrafting service as sustainability through keeping shoes in use instead of replacing them.

labor.note: Allen Edmonds says its shoes are handcrafted in Port Washington, Wisconsin, but parent-company labor disclosure is not as strong as union or fair-trade proof.

transparency.note: The recrafting FAQ explains what can and cannot be repaired, including limits around uppers and non-recraftable construction.

durability.note: Allen Edmonds' 360-degree Goodyear bench welt allows many pairs to be refurbished by brand experts when they show wear.

accessibility.note: Allen Edmonds is widely available in the US for dress and casual shoes, but upfront prices and recrafting costs are premium.

products.description: A dress-shoe repairability benchmark: expensive and leather-based, but explicitly built around recrafting and long service life.

products.name: Shein / Temu shoes

environment.note: Greenpeace describes Shein and Temu as ultra-fast-fashion platforms adding thousands of low-price styles and normalizing disposable consumption.

labor.note: Eco-Stylist's 2026 avoid list flags fast fashion for low pricing tied to weak labor standards and names both SHEIN and Temu among major culprits.

transparency.note: Eco-Stylist's 2026 criteria for its avoid list include lack of supply-chain transparency, high synthetic/virgin-material reliance and overconsumption pressure.

durability.note: Ultra-fast-fashion platforms normalize disposable clothing culture, so cheap shoes from the same marketplaces are weak on repair, resoling and long use.

accessibility.note: The main advantage is extreme affordability and marketplace availability, which is why this remains the honest floor.

products.description: Ultra-cheap platform shoes from Shein/Temu-style marketplaces: very accessible, but the clearest floor for labor, quality and transparency.

products.name: Nike Refurbished

environment.note: Nike Refurbished is explicitly designed to keep returned shoes in use longer through resale, donation or recycling instead of landfill.

labor.note: Refurbishing extends use but does not change the underlying labor profile of Nike's original global footwear supply chain.

transparency.note: Nike describes the program categories as like-new, gently worn and cosmetically flawed returned footwear that is cleaned and resold.

durability.note: The route gives wearable returned shoes another life, though it is not the same as designing every pair for resoling or repair.

accessibility.note: The program is attached to participating Nike stores, so access is useful but much narrower than ordinary new Nike retail.

products.description: A practical lower-waste route for people who still want Nike sneakers, with the caveat that refurbishing does not fix the whole supply chain.

products.name: R.M.Williams boots

environment.note: R.M.Williams frames its sustainability strategy around long-lived products that can be repaired repeatedly rather than replaced quickly.

labor.note: The brand says its boots have been handcrafted in Australia since 1932, and B Lab lists R.M.Williams as B Corp certified.

transparency.note: R.M.Williams publishes a sustainability strategy and B Corp profile, giving more public governance and impact detail than most heritage boot brands.

durability.note: The company says Goodyear welted construction allows boots to be broken down and worn components replaced without compromising structure.

accessibility.note: The boots are globally recognized but premium-priced, so this is a durability route rather than an affordability route.

products.description: A high-durability boot benchmark: expensive and leather-based, but unusually strong on recrafting, local manufacturing signals and public B Corp accountability.

products.name: The Captain boot

environment.note: Thursday reports traceable leather sourcing and Leather Working Group-rated tanneries, but the product remains leather footwear with limited circularity detail.

labor.note: The brand publishes sourcing values and tannery claims, but less third-party worker-wage evidence than top labor-transparent footwear brands.

transparency.note: Thursday names Tier 1 USA cattle sourcing and LWG-rated tanneries, while The Commons still rates the broader sustainability disclosure as incomplete.

durability.note: The Captain product page says the boot uses Goodyear welt construction, which supports resoling and longer service life.

accessibility.note: Thursday is much more affordable than many welted heritage boots, though still costly compared with mall-fashion shoes.

products.description: A mid-price bridge into repairable welted boots: better durability than disposable fashion shoes, but not a top labor-transparency leader.

products.name: Camper

environment.note: Camper publishes sustainability reports and circular-design work, including recyclable and repairable/replacement-part product initiatives.

labor.note: B Lab lists Camper Group as B Corp certified with a 97.8 impact score across governance, workers, community, environment and customers.

transparency.note: Camper says it publishes annual sustainability reports to share strategy, progress and challenges.

durability.note: Camper highlights lifetime-guarantee styles, ReCrafted, Second Life and shoe-care initiatives, though not every model is fully repairable.

accessibility.note: B Lab lists Camper as operating across the US, UK, EU and other markets, making it more accessible than many niche ethical footwear brands.

products.description: A globally available casual-footwear B Corp with stronger transparency and circular-design work than most mall shoe brands.

products.name: La Sportiva

environment.note: La Sportiva says its authorized-resoler network preserves product performance while limiting environmental impact.

labor.note: The available resole and product-performance evidence is stronger than the public worker-wage evidence, so labor is scored cautiously.

transparency.note: The brand publishes an authorized-resoler network and repair guidance, but less whole-supply-chain disclosure than top transparency leaders.

durability.note: Since 2012 La Sportiva has operated authorized resolers using original spare parts across more than ten European markets.

accessibility.note: This is specialist technical footwear; accessibility is strongest for climbers and hikers near authorized repair routes, not general shoppers.

products.description: A technical climbing and mountain-footwear option where resoling can materially extend use, especially for users already in the outdoor category.

products.name: SCARPA

environment.note: SCARPA frames its Long Life Design around reducing impact through durable, repairable and resoleable products.

labor.note: SCARPA's repairability evidence is stronger than its public worker-wage evidence, so the labor score remains moderate.

transparency.note: The brand publishes a resole project and US service-center list, giving concrete repair-path visibility for technical footwear.

durability.note: SCARPA says repairability and resoling arise from boot and climbing-shoe construction designed for longevity from the start.

accessibility.note: SCARPA is a specialist outdoor brand with repair centers, but it is less affordable and less general-purpose than mainstream shoe brands.

products.description: A mountain-footwear durability entry: not cheap or universal, but a strong example of designing technical shoes and boots to be resoled.

products.name: Steve Madden

environment.note: Good On You rates Steve Madden 'Not Good Enough' for planet, citing few lower-impact materials and weak hazardous-chemical action.

labor.note: Good On You rates Steve Madden 'Not Good Enough' for people, noting no evidence that it ensures living wages in its supply chain.

transparency.note: Steve Madden publishes a sustainability strategy, but independent ratings still flag gaps in supply-chain and impact disclosure.

durability.note: The brand's public sustainability materials emphasize packaging and strategy rather than repair, resoling or long-life construction.

accessibility.note: Steve Madden is highly recognizable and widely sold through retail and online channels, making it an important mall-fashion benchmark.

products.description: A recognizable mall-fashion shoe floor: easy to find, but weak on independent environmental, labor and repairability signals.

products.name: ALDO

environment.note: ALDO reports FSC-certified shoeboxes with at least 80% recycled fibers and some lower-impact material initiatives, but remains a mainstream fashion-footwear retailer.

labor.note: ALDO publishes CSR and sourcing efforts, but independent summaries still flag limited evidence on deeper labor outcomes such as living wages.

transparency.note: The brand has more public CSR disclosure than many mall-fashion peers, including climate and sourcing initiatives, but not top-tier product traceability.

durability.note: ALDO's public sustainability page emphasizes packaging, materials and carbon initiatives more than repairable or resoleable construction.

accessibility.note: ALDO's global retail and online footprint makes it a practical benchmark for shoppers comparing everyday fashion shoes.

products.description: A mainstream fashion-footwear benchmark with some public sustainability work, but weaker durability and labor proof than repair-first brands.

products.name: Red Wing Repair Shop

environment.note: Red Wing says repairing before wear turns into damage is one of the best ways to extend boot life.

labor.note: The repair shop keeps cobbler work inside Red Wing's Minnesota repair operation and local partner network.

transparency.note: Red Wing publishes a repair menu with package and a la carte services including resoles, heels, stitching, eyelets and gussets.

durability.note: The official repair page says welt-constructed Red Wing boots can often be repaired, while damaged leather or linings may limit eligibility.

accessibility.note: Users can bring boots to a Red Wing store or contact customer service for a shipping label on qualifying paid services, but the service is brand-limited.

products.description: A strong brand-backed repair route for Red Wing owners: high on longevity and craft, limited to repairable Red Wing-family boots.

products.name: Danner Recrafting

environment.note: Danner says repairing boots extends their life and keeps them out of landfill, preserving the broken-in fit while replacing worn components.

labor.note: Danner describes recrafting as hand rebuild work by its Portland recrafters using the machines the boots were originally built with.

transparency.note: The page lists the process, current turnaround, prices for rebuild/resole packages and explicit eligibility limits.

durability.note: Danner's resole service can replace soles, recondition leather, repair stitching and hardware, and add new laces.

accessibility.note: The service uses an online assessment and mail-in process, but cost, boot eligibility and leather condition limit universal access.

products.description: A high-value option when Danner boots still fit and the uppers qualify: more expensive than DIY care, much less wasteful than default replacement.

products.name: Allen Edmonds Recrafting

environment.note: Allen Edmonds frames recrafting as sustainability through keeping favorite footwear rather than letting it go.

labor.note: The service is tied to its Port Washington, Wisconsin studio and expert restoration work using original-style materials and lasts.

transparency.note: Allen Edmonds publishes package details, pricing, eligibility checks and limits, including that it only recrafts Allen Edmonds shoes.

durability.note: The brand says its 360-degree Goodyear bench welt lets experts refurbish many pairs when they show signs of wear.

accessibility.note: Recrafting is useful for qualifying dress shoes and boots, but the service is premium-priced and not every Allen Edmonds style qualifies.

products.description: A concrete recrafting path for repairable Allen Edmonds pairs, especially dress shoes where a new sole can beat a new purchase.

products.name: R.M.Williams boot repair service

environment.note: R.M.Williams repairs can replace sole and heel components or fully resole boots when regular wear has worn them down.

labor.note: The brand describes repairs as being restored by the same hands that crafted the boots, preserving repair labor rather than replacing the pair.

transparency.note: The repair page names specific services such as heel/sole replacement, elastics, tugs, relasting and sole-type constraints.

durability.note: Its relast service can remanufacture the boot while retaining the upper leather, lining, tugs and elastics when eligible.

accessibility.note: Repair requires stores or licensed repairers and eligible uppers, so this is powerful for owners but not a low-friction mass-market route.

products.description: A premium boot-life-extension route: strong repair depth for eligible R.M.Williams boots, but tied to brand access and high upfront footwear cost.

products.name: Fit refresh: insoles and laces

environment.note: Replacing the small parts that affect fit can keep an otherwise usable pair in rotation instead of sending it to replacement early.

labor.note: This is not a labor-certification route; it is a low-material maintenance choice using commodity replacement parts.

transparency.note: REI's boot guidance explicitly recommends considering aftermarket insoles to improve comfort, support or fit.

durability.note: Replacement laces and insoles address common failure and comfort points without replacing the whole shoe.

accessibility.note: Laces and insoles are low-cost and widely available compared with resoling or brand recrafting.

products.description: The simplest repair-adjacent move: swap laces or insoles before declaring a pair uncomfortable, tired or finished.

products.name: Shoe Goo minor repair adhesive

environment.note: Shoe Goo can fix worn soles or damaged heels and coat shoes to prevent premature wear, reducing some early replacement.

labor.note: DIY adhesive repair saves a pair cheaply, but it does not support skilled cobbler labor the way professional repair does.

transparency.note: The product page states intended uses and material compatibility, but provides less lifecycle or chemical-depth disclosure than repair services.

durability.note: The adhesive is designed for abrasion resistance and flexible-material adhesion, useful for small sole and heel repairs.

accessibility.note: Shoe Goo is a cheap, mainstream DIY fix for small failures, though not a substitute for structural repair or resoling.

products.description: A practical floor for small failures: not a cobbler, not a resole, but often enough to keep a worn sole or heel from becoming a same-day replacement.

products.name: Gear Aid Aquaseal SR

environment.note: Aquaseal SR is aimed at repairing cracked soles, worn toe caps, loose soles and waterproof high-wear areas rather than replacing the shoe.

labor.note: As a DIY repair adhesive, it shifts work to the user rather than cobbler labor, so the labor score stays modest.

transparency.note: Gear Aid publishes material, size, cure time, use temperature, adhesion materials and a California warning on the product page.

durability.note: The adhesive dries as a clear flexible glue and is designed to withstand heat, cold and heavy-duty footwear use.

accessibility.note: A small tube is affordable and field-friendly, but it requires curing time and judgment about whether the shoe needs professional repair instead.

products.description: A sturdier outdoor-oriented DIY repair route for loose soles, toe caps and boot damage, with chemical-use caveats and curing-time friction.

products.name: Nikwax footwear cleaning and proofing

environment.note: Nikwax Footwear Cleaning Gel is PFAS-free and designed to restore water repellency and breathability without aerosol application.

labor.note: Footwear care is not a labor-justice standout, but extending outdoor shoe life can reduce replacement demand.

transparency.note: The product page states suitability, use steps, PFAS-free status and when cleaning alone is not enough and reproofing is needed.

durability.note: Nikwax explains that dirt can mask durable water repellency, and cleaning can revitalize DWR and breathability for waterproof footwear.

accessibility.note: The cleaner is easy to apply by hand and widely sold in outdoor retail, though it is most relevant to waterproof footwear rather than all shoes.

products.description: A care route for waterproof boots and shoes: best when dirt and wetting-out are making a still-useful pair feel worse than it is.
